Her family, Chief George Cote, Senator Mary Jane McCallum and MP Jenica Atwin helped bring national attention to respect for Indigenous cultural expression. The incident, the law and the later commemoration must not be conflated.

en.heading: 8 January: a national memorial for air-disaster victims

The date is the anniversary of the downing of flight PS752 near Tehran in 2020, when all 176 people aboard died. The original order also mentions Air India 182 and Ethiopian Airlines 302, making clear that the remembrance extends beyond one tragedy. The first annual commemoration followed in 2021; the order is not proof of a federal paid public holiday.

en.heading: 11 January: a day to study Canada's first prime minister
en.origin: Sir John A. Macdonald Day takes place on 11 January, the anniversary of Canada's first prime minister's birth. The Sir John A. Macdonald Day and Sir Wilfrid Laurier Day Act came into force in March 2002, long after the Confederation that Macdonald helped establish in 1867. The date and the statute belong to the modern commemoration, not to the country's founding. Canadian Heritage encourages schools and communities to examine Canadian political history. A balanced understanding also considers the harmful consequences of colonial policies in Macdonald's era. No original first ceremony is proven by the cited overview.

en.heading: 17 January: remembering Raoul Wallenberg
en.origin: Raoul Wallenberg Day honours the Swedish diplomat whose protective documents and shelters helped persecuted Jews in Nazi-occupied Hungary. It falls on 17 January because Wallenberg was taken into Soviet custody on that day in 1945 and subsequently disappeared. Canadian government materials disagree about the recognition year: a ministerial statement gives 2001, while another Canadian Heritage page mentions a parliamentary declaration in 2002. The founding field therefore stays unknown pending inspection of the original act. Wallenberg became an honorary Canadian citizen in 1985. The day commemorates humanitarian courage, not the arrest itself.

en.purpose: Recall humanitarian rescue during the Holocaust and reject antisemitism and persecution.

L'anno istitutivo resta quindi sconosciuto fino alla verifica del provvedimento originario. Il Canada gli conferì la cittadinanza onoraria nel 1985.

en.heading: 21 January: honouring Lincoln Alexander's public service
en.origin: Lincoln Alexander Day was created through Bill S-213, introduced in the Senate in December 2013 by Senator Don Meredith and sponsored in the Commons by MP David Sweet. The legislation passed in 2014, and federal statements describe 21 January 2015 as the first national celebration. The birthday anniversary honours Canada's first Black member of Parliament, who also served in the federal Cabinet and as Ontario's lieutenant governor. His career illustrates both political achievement and the barriers imposed by racial discrimination. The 2014 act and the first annual event in 2015 are different milestones.

en.purpose: Celebrate Black Canadian leadership, civic contribution and progress toward equality.
